items_missed: Section 1 (Set Agenda): never got or used the customer's name, never asked how she was doing, and gave no real agenda statement or 'sound good?' confirmation before diving into questions.
Section 2 (Probe): never asked about storage stops or whether she had any worries/stressors about the move.
Section 3 (Pricing): no mention of No Worries Damage Coverage, no Meet Your Mover email, and no On-Time Guarantee.
Section 5 (Estimate): the 50-60ft walk distance he asked about was never tied back into the time explanation, and no equivalents/analogy were used to make the estimate concrete.
Section 6 (Save Your Ass): skipped entirely — no prep-shortens-the-move framing, no consolidation examples, no 'take a carload' tip.
Section 7 (Quote/Booking): no confirmation email mentioned at all, so no bolded detail list and no 'reply with corrections' either, and he never gave office hours or how to reach the team.
Section 8 (Politeness): never used the customer's name once — she was only addressed as 'ma'am' at the close.
Section 9 (Bonus): no rapport-building or humor moment, and the insurance explanation (No Worries + 60 cents/lb baseline) was never given.
top_strength: Joel ran the clock and pricing mechanics cleanly and confidently — "Our pricing is super simple. We charge $218 an hour for a two man crew, everything's already included" — and he made a smart, specific adjustment: he proactively added 30 minutes to the auto-quoted time because the destination bedroom was on the third floor, then explained why.
coaching_note: Joel, the mechanics — clock, minimum, proration, hourly rate — were all clean and accurate. But you skipped every differentiator that actually justifies the price: no Save Your Ass prep speech, no Meet Your Mover, no On-Time Guarantee, no damage coverage. Use the customer's name a few times instead of 'ma'am' — it's a courtesy call about her own upcoming move, and it should feel personal, not like a data intake form. And always close with a confirmation email and how to reach you; right now she hangs up with a number and nothing in writing.
phone_presence_notes: Polite and professional throughout but transactional — no name use, no empathy when she apologized for not knowing her square footage, and the pricing/clock explanation ran as a monologue rather than a conversation.
